01 / An exact counterexample to generic confinement

The disk gains a second zero
before the pair collides.

Exact polynomial model

Reflection symmetry pins a unique zero in a reflection-symmetric disk to the critical line. That conclusion depends on the disk continuing to contain exactly one zero. In this quartet, another zero enters first.

02 / The actual theta heat family

Three roots move in height.
No sideways motion is resolved.

Numerical evidence

Continue the first three ξ zeros into the theta heat family, starting at τ = 0. Their height changes are visible; their sampled real parts remain at σ = ½. The absence of a numerical departure does not exclude unsampled or other off-line zeros.

A diagnostic, with a precise limit

The sampled barrier stays positive.

A small bridge must be small
relative to the distance from the zero.

Actual heat source · τ = −0.2

What follows from the comparison

Keep the hypothesis
with the conclusion.

01

Isolation has content.

A reflection-symmetric region containing exactly one zero, counted with multiplicity, forces that zero onto the symmetry line. The quartet shows that this premise can fail before collision.

02

A sampled barrier is evidence.

The theta tracks and contour margins are consistent with local confinement in the tested runs. They do not certify every boundary arc, every time, or the absence of other zeros.

03

The bridge has a scale.

The finite difference and the analytic derivative answer related questions. Their agreement near a zero requires a small shift relative to that zero’s distance.

This comparison supplies an exact calibration and concrete numerical checks. It does not prove the Riemann Hypothesis.
